title: Residue index
definition: Places where English Bibles, or the witnesses behind them, disagree in a way that looks like something used to be there.

items.english_collision: KJV / JPS: 'sons of Israel' or 'Israel's numbers'. Brenton: 'angels of God'. Modern eclectic English sometimes: 'sons of God' / 'gods'.
items.hypothesis: English is tracking a Hebrew fork (ישראל vs אלהים), not a translator whim.

items.english_collision: KJV: nations rejoice; no gods. Brenton / some modern English: heavens and sons/angels of God worship. Hebrews 1:6 still quotes the longer Greek line.
items.hypothesis: Masoretic ending is shorter. Residue survives in Greek English and in the New Testament citation.

items.english_collision: KJV prints the longer ending. ASV and later critical English often bracket or footnote it. This is the reverse of the Deuteronomy pattern: here the older English is longer.
items.hypothesis: English is tracking Greek manuscript streams (Byzantine/TR vs early Alexandrian copies), not a modern conspiracy.

items.english_collision: KJV: three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost. ASV and most later English drop the heavenly witnesses.
items.hypothesis: Latin residue that entered late Greek and then English. Confirm on Greek/Latin intake; do not decide from English alone.

items.english_collision: KJV has the eunuch's confession. Most later English skip from 8:36 to 8:38.
items.hypothesis: TR / Western expansion vs shorter Alexandrian text. English collision is clean.

items.english_collision: KJV: 'they pierced my hands and my feet.' JPS 1917: 'like a lion, my hands and my feet.' Versification also shifts.
items.hypothesis: כארו / כארי plus Christian vs Jewish English. Versification residue on the side.

items.english_collision: Jude in every English NT quotes Enoch as prophecy. 1 Enoch is absent from KJV, JPS, and most Protestant/Catholic tables of contents; present in the Ethiopian canon.
items.hypothesis: Canon residue, not a verse variant. English NT still carries the quotation after the book left the Western list.

items.english_collision: 1611 KJV bound Wisdom, Sirach, 1–2 Maccabees, and the rest between the testaments. Later Protestant printings often omit the section entirely.
items.hypothesis: Print-history residue. Douay keeps a related set as deuterocanon. Compare on English intake before Greek/Latin.
